name: Notion (sign-in wrapper)
description: Notion's official hosted MCP server with built-in sign-in. Adds login, status and logout tools in front of mcp.notion.com, so the user signs in through Notion's own browser flow without creating an app or token. Search, read and edit pages, databases and task lists. Use for 'sign in to Notion', 'find my meeting notes', 'add a task', 'update that page'.
summary: Search, read and edit your Notion pages, databases and task lists, through Notion's official hosted server and a browser sign-in

transports.description: Notion wrapper (stdio): sign-in tools plus a relay to Notion's hosted server.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Sign in to Notion. Prints a sign-in link, opens the browser, and blocks until the user approves, declines or it times out. Dispatch it as a concurrent task with a reminder, and tell the user to open the link when it appears in the output. The user chooses which pages Notion shares during sign-in. The token is never returned.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Report whether JARVIS is signed in to Notion. No network call.

tools.name: logout
tools.description: Forget the stored Notion sign-in on this machine. Does not revoke it at Notion.

tools.name: notion-search
tools.description: Search the workspace's pages and databases by keyword, location, author, date or status.

tools.name: notion-fetch
tools.description: Read a page, database, data source or saved view by URL or ID.

tools.name: notion-create-pages
tools.description: Create one or more pages with properties, content, icon and cover.

tools.name: notion-update-page
tools.description: Change a page's properties, content, icon, cover or Skill status.

tools.name: notion-query-data-sources
tools.description: Query database rows with SQL, or run a saved view.

tools.name: notion-create-database
tools.description: Create a database with properties and an initial view.

tools.name: notion-update-data-source
tools.description: Change a database's schema: its properties, name or description. Removing a property drops that column's data across every row.

tools.name: notion-create-view
tools.description: Create a database view (table, board, calendar, timeline, and others).

tools.name: notion-update-view
tools.description: Change a view's name, filters, sorts or layout.

tools.name: notion-ai-search
tools.description: Natural-language search across Notion and the sources connected to it (Slack, mail, calendar, Google Drive, Jira).

tools.name: notion-query-meeting-notes
tools.description: Query the current user's meeting notes by their properties.

tools.name: notion-create-comment
tools.description: Comment on a page, a block, or an existing discussion.

tools.name: notion-get-comments
tools.description: List the comments and discussions on a page.

tools.name: notion-move-pages
tools.description: Move pages or databases under a new parent.

tools.name: notion-duplicate-page
tools.description: Copy a page within the workspace.

tools.name: notion-create-folder
tools.description: Create an empty folder under a page.

tools.name: notion-get-users
tools.description: List workspace members and guests with their contact details.

tools.name: notion-get-teams
tools.description: List the teamspaces in the workspace.

tools.name: notion-create-attachment
tools.description: Create an attachment from text, a public URL, or a finished upload.

tools.name: notion-download-attachment
tools.description: Download the text of an attachment (up to 200 KiB).

tools.name: notion-get-tool-access
tools.description: Report which tools the workspace's plan allows and which parameters are restricted.

tools.name: notion-get-async-task
tools.description: Check the status of an operation another tool started asynchronously.

tools.name: notion-download-skill
tools.description: Download a Notion Skill and its files as a tar.gz archive.

tools.name: notion-convert-page-to-skill
tools.description: Mark a page as a Notion Skill without changing its content.

tools.name: notion-create-file-upload
tools.description: Create a short-lived URL for uploading a local file to Notion.

tools.name: notion-list-agents
tools.description: List the workspace's Custom Agents.

tools.name: notion-search-agents
tools.description: Find a Custom Agent's URL, needed to start a session with it.

tools.name: notion-query-sessions
tools.description: List Custom Agent sessions.

tools.name: notion-search-sessions
tools.description: Search past Custom Agent sessions.

tools.name: notion-get-session-status
tools.description: Get a Custom Agent session's current status.

tools.name: notion-list-session-events
tools.description: List the events of a Custom Agent session.

tools.name: notion-read-session-event
tools.description: Read one event of a Custom Agent session.

tools.name: notion-wait-session
tools.description: Wait for a Custom Agent session to finish.

tools.name: notion-spawn-session
tools.description: Start a Custom Agent session. The agent acts in the workspace, and its connected tools, on its own.

tools.name: notion-send-message-to-session
tools.description: Send a follow-up instruction to a running Custom Agent session.

tools.name: notion-stop-session
tools.description: Stop a running Custom Agent session.

checks: vendor: first-party, hosted by Notion at mcp.notion.com; the wrapper runs locally and relays to it
wrapper: first-party stdlib Python in this repository; shared sign-in helper vendored from servers/_lib, identical copy enforced by the PR gate

auth: MCP authorization spec, checked live 2026-10-12: protected-resource metadata names mcp.notion.com as authorization server; dynamic client registration; PKCE S256; public clients; scopes_supported [default]
network: HTTPS to mcp.notion.com only; discovered endpoints and redirects are host-pinned
secrets: the token is stored in the OS keyring (secret-tool) or an owner-only file; it is never returned in a tool result or logged
access: the integration only sees the pages and databases the user shares with it during sign-in

tools: 36 from Notion's supported-tools page plus login/status/logout; some are plan-restricted (notion-get-tool-access reports which); rate limits: notion-search and notion-query-data-sources, 20 calls per 10 seconds
trust.notes: Replaces the draft mcp-registry#105 entry, which relied on dmcp's hosted sign-in (dmcp#70); under design v3 the wrapper owns the sign-in and dmcp stays generic. The tool list is Notion's documentation, not a live tools/list: after the first sign-in, compare the live list with it. A tool missing here is still gated, at elevated, by JARVIS's registry-tier floor. Linux and macOS only until the token store has a Windows backend.
trust.securityNotes: Reads are elevated because page content, comments and ai-search results can carry text anyone with edit access wrote (prompt-injection surface). Page edits are elevated rather than dangerous because Notion keeps page history. Schema changes and Custom Agent sessions are dangerous: the first can drop a property's data across a whole database, the second hands an autonomous agent the workspace and its connected tools.
